messages:
sarah_support: FYI ACME is seeing intermittent 500s from /v1/generate and says there is no request-id in their logs or the response headers. They attached a screenshot but we need a reproducible trace. Can someone confirm the minimal set of artifacts to ask them for?

mike_eng: Minimal ask: 1) a HAR (or Copy as cURL) from the client that shows the failing request, 2) the full response headers (not just body), and 3) the SDK debug/session token visible in logs (we call it the edge-session / req-ref). If a proxy is involved, we need upstream proxy headers/logs too.

customer_acme: I can do the cURL step — how do I include headers? My browser network panel doesn't show X-Request-ID.

sarah_support: For browser: DevTools -> Network -> reproduce -> right-click the failing request -> "Save all as HAR" OR "Copy -> Copy as cURL". Attach the HAR file or paste the copied cURL (remove your auth token). Also in the right-hand pane click "Headers" and paste the full response headers section.

mike_eng: For a quick, safe curl you can run locally (replace token with <REDACTED> before sharing):

```
curl -i -X POST 'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_TOKEN>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' -s
```

That will print response headers and body. Paste the headers block exactly as returned. If the response has no X-Request-ID header, paste the full header list — that helps us detect proxies or header stripping.

mike_eng: Mobile (Android) quick-tip: run `adb logcat | grep -i redwood` while reproducing; look for lines that include "edge-session" or "req_ref" or "debug_ticket". On iOS, ask for the console logs (macOS Console app) while reproducing.

mike_eng: If you suspect a proxy (Cloudflare, custom gateway, mobile carrier), ask the customer to include a unique header on their request so we can correlate. e.g., set `X-CUSTOM-REQ: my-test-1234` on the client side, reproduce, then send that value plus any proxy logs. Some gateways rewrite or drop X-Request-ID; a custom header helps.

customer_acme: We use an internal gateway — I'll try adding a header and send the HAR. One question: where in the console would I find the SDK session token you mentioned?

sarah_support: In the Redwood SDK console: open the app -> Settings -> Debug -> Enable verbose logs -> reproduce a request -> Console shows an "edge-session" (or "req-ref") string. Alternatively, in browser logs you may see `redwood.session` or `X-Redwood-Debug` printed. Copy that exact token and attach it. If you can't enable verbose logs, send the HAR + cURL and we'll look for anything we can correlate.

mike_eng: If you already have a HAR, you can also grep it for "requestId", "x-request-id", "edge-session", "session_ref", or any long hex strings — paste the surrounding lines. If HAR redacts auth, still useful.

customer_acme: Attaching HAR and copy-as-curl now (token redacted) — headers show HTTP/1.1 500 and Date, Content-Type, Server only. No request id. I also added X-CUSTOM-REQ: acme-test-2026 in the header.

sarah_support: Received, thanks. I'll escalate to eng-oncall with the HAR + the acme-test-2026 marker. If we need more, eng will ask for upstream gateway logs.

deploy-bot: deployment/2026-03-17-218 completed :rocket:

customer_acme: Thanks, ping me if you need anything else. :thumbsup:
